newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan may take Indonesia car issue to WTO Friday.
newsitem.headline: Japan may take Indonesia car issue to WTO Friday.

text.p: Japan plans to complain to the World Trade Organisation (WTO) over Indonesia's national car policy as early as Friday, Minister of International Trade and Industry Shunpei Tsukahara told a news conference.
MITI officials said earlier this week that Japan would take the complaints to the WTO, forming a united front with its traditional trade adversary, the United States.

Jakarta's national car plan, announced earlier this year, has come under fire from Japan, the United States and Europe as a violation of world trade rules. Indonesia said in February that a firm controlled by President Suharto's youngest son would get tax breaks to make sedans in collaboration with South Korea's Kia Motors.

Tsukahara said Japan had decided to make the complaint to the world trade body after asking Indonesia three times to make the national car plan conform with international trade rules. He added that both countries wanted to keep the trade dispute from harming friendly ties.
On Thursday, the European Union also said it had decided to launch a formal complaint to the WTO on Indonesia's car policy.
